As you know kidney crystals are formed in the kidneys and the crystals then form the urine. The crystals become more and more concentrated in a stone as they grow. When the stone is in your bladder the fluid is very concentrated. Black spots are caused by crystals that have hardened. If the stones are small and your urine is also clear then the black spot is not very serious. But if the number of black crystals is more than one per cent of your stone then you are more at risk of kidney damage. A urine sample should be taken to check for stones and if you have more black stones than your own urine then call your doctor. Most of the time stones in large stones will be found. Sometimes you will have to take a urine test to see if stones have formed. This is called a urodynamic urine analysis. It is important to pay attention to the size of stones as stones of less than two inches in size are usually harmless. About 10 percent of people have stones larger than this. In rare cases large crystals can cause kidney failure. You should call if your stones grow to more then two and a half inches. Please contact me if it is your first time. Thank you for your time!

You may feel as though you are going to die.Although a warning sign, this is also a sign of an imminent heart problem because it can signal the death of one or both of two heart valves.A heart condition called Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome (WPW) is caused by an abnormality in a single heart valve. WPW occurs when the valve is damaged, not by blood clots, as in Wolffe's disease, which is common in older people.WP Ws often have symptoms such as shortness of breath, palpitations, chest pain, muscle weakness and fatigue. view entire post The test is to check your heart's electrical activity and determine if you have a blockage. If it is blocked, then you need to have the block removed. A blockages can cause a cardiac arrest, which is very bad and you will need emergency surgery to save your life. It is important to know that you can have heart attacks even if your blood pressure is low. The heart has an electrical signal to keep it pumping and blood flowing. There is no way to tell if this electrical "signal" is being sent correctly. This is why the doctor's are so concerned about your health. He will have you take a blood test to see if there is an abnormality in the electrical signals sent to your body by the heart. An abnormally low blood-pressure can lead to a dangerous heart rhythm. So if the blood tests show an abnormal electrical rhythm, the medical team will take you to the emergency room. You will be given medications to help keep your oxygen levels up so you are awake and alert during the surgery, so that if an emergency happens you won't pass out. Then you should be allowed to go home and rest for 10-15 days. Sometimes, if a person has a blocked heart, he or she needs a pacemaker implanted to give the normal electrical pulses to their heart and keep them from having a sudden cardiac event. Answer:
. . . The venom of a female orb web spider has no known harmful effects on humans or animals.
The venom is similar in composition to that of the black widow spider and is a natural component of their webs. The spider's venom has a chemical that is very similar to a nerve gas, called neuromuscular blocking toxin (NMTB). The toxin blocks a muscle that normally helps the spider to grip its web. This means that if the web is cut or damaged, the female spider can not hold on to the material. If the bite is severe enough, she will die from the resulting infection.
If you think your spider is infected with a venomous spider, you should see a doctor. You will likely need to have a blood test and possibly be given anti-venom. However, there is no evidence that there are any serious side effects from a bite from an orb spider. There is, however, a rare but potentially dangerous complication associated with the bites of an infected spider: necrotic arachnidism (NA). This is an infection of tissues of your armpit, where the abdomen of spiders is located. Necrotized tissues can lead to necrosis and scarring. It is rare, and requires immediate medical attention. In addition to being very painful, necrotysis can also cause paralysis of muscles that control breathing. Your doctor may prescribe medication for this condition.
